entries.rationale: The run reproduced a real authoring hazard: an enumerated set of candidates does not prove exhaustive closure. Existing requirements and one_of semantics already require relationship-level grounding, so boundary case 3 was clarified to keep the variable open until a separate cited span explicitly closes it. This aligns documentation with contract 0.1 and does not change grammar, schemas, or semantics.

The complete read path makes declaration, variable, candidate, constraint, and one-record inspection available. Grouping by frozen dogfood question is process-specific rather than a stable semantic result, while expanding arbitrary grounding graphs would anticipate the separately gated explain contract. Phase 2 acceptance does not justify a new filter route or public result shape.

The status text is stale for the current private implementation, but requirements.md is part of the protocol-v1 corpus and the completed receipt intentionally binds its old digest. Preserve that evidence and update the status only when the next CSP dogfood round establishes protocol v2 and a new corpus baseline.

The observed output preserves authored grounding and domain closure without producing support-state or viability classifications. This is the required Phase 2 boundary; candidate viability, exclusion chains, and unknown reasons remain Phase 3 work.

point_adjustments.rationale: Synchronize the coarse Phase 2 slice with the current detailed plan total, including the accepted jscpd gate and both dogfood feedback reviews, without converting points into elapsed time.
Reserve 2p to create the next versioned corpus baseline, update the stale requirements status, and preserve protocol-v1 receipt identity before the CSP dogfood rerun.
